papers.title: Stain Normalisation Does Not Consistently Improve Matched-Location Retrieval with Pathology Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Pathology foundation models provide reusable representations for computational pathology, but staining- and scanner-induced variation may compromise the robustness and reproducibility of embedding-based analyses across acquisition settings. Stain normalisation is widely used to mitigate such colour variation, yet whether it improves retrieval with modern self-supervised pathology encoders remains unclear. We test whether stain normalisation improves cross-scanner and cross-staining image retrieval using the PLISM whole-slide image subset, comprising 13 co-registered images of serial sections prepared under different staining conditions and digitised using seven scanners (91 whole-slide images). We sample 400 matched locations across the 91 images, yielding 36,400 tile instances. We compare two DINOv2-based encoders, Phikon-v2 (1,024-dimensional) and Midnight-12k (3,072-dimensional), with Reinhard and Macenko normalisation against an unnormalised baseline. Performance is measured using paired top-1 nearest-neighbour retrieval accuracy in two settings: cross-scanner retrieval of the same physical section digitised by different scanners, and cross-staining retrieval across co-registered images of serial sections, which differ in staining condition and may also contain section-level morphological variation. Neither normalisation method consistently improves top-1 retrieval relative to no normalisation, while Macenko reduces accuracy by up to 18.3 percentage points. An exploratory UMAP of unnormalised Midnight-12k slide-level mean embeddings showed partial overlap between scanner groups in a two-dimensional projection. These results challenge the routine use of stain normalisation in foundation-model retrieval pipelines and support validating preprocessing choices for each encoder and retrieval setting.

papers.title: Phylogenomic Characterization of Two Alternaria Lineages Associated with Cotton Leaf Spot in Tennessee
papers.abstract: Alternaria leaf spot is an important foliar disease of cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) and has historically been associated primarily with Alternaria macrospora in the United States. In November 2025, symptomatic Upland cotton leaves from a research greenhouse at Tennessee Technological University's Oakley Farm in Livingston, Tennessee, yielded two Alternaria isolates, 2-2 and 9-1. Quantitative conidial characterization showed substantial overlap in dimensions, septation, and shape. Concatenated ITS-RPB2 phylogenetic analysis supported different broad affinities, placing isolate 2-2 within an A. alternata- dominated group and isolate 9-1 within a group associated with the A. arborescens species complex (AASC), although their immediate relationships were weakly resolved. Phylogenomic analysis of 1,501 single-copy BUSCO orthologs from 63 genomes placed isolate 2-2 within the A. alternata lineage, sister to BMP2343, and isolate 9-1 within the AASC, sister to MOD1-FUNGI6. In controlled pathogenicity assays, isolate 9-1 reproduced foliar lesions on cotton, whereas mock-inoculated plants remained symptomless, and molecularly confirmed re-isolation fulfilled Koch's postulates. Isolate 2-2 produced insufficient conidia under the culture conditions used to prepare a standardized inoculum, and its pathogenicity was therefore not determined. These results reveal phylogenetically distinct Alternaria lineages associated with symptomatic cotton and establish an AASC isolate as a causal agent of cotton leaf spot in Tennessee.

papers.title: Pathological musculoskeletal characterisation of a new model of spontaneous OA in CD1 mice.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a whole joint disease involving pathological changes in cartilage, synovium, ligaments, menisci and periarticular muscle. This study provides a comprehensive musculoskeletal characterisation of spontaneous OA in male CD1 mice to evaluate their suitability as a model of naturally occurring disease. Knee joints from 3-4 and 6-8 month old mice were analysed histologically, OARSI scoring and immunohistochemistry for markers of chondrogenesis and endochondral ossification. Quadriceps and gastrocnemius muscles were examined for fibre cross sectional area. CD1 mice displayed mild OA at 3-4 months, progressing to moderate to severe disease by 6-8 months. Cartilage loss, synovial hyperplasia and fibrosis increased across compartments. Anterior cruciate and collateral ligaments, and medial meniscus exhibited marked pathological remodelling, including proteoglycan rich rounded cell regions and evidence of endochondral ossification with increased COL2, SOX9, RUNX2 and ASPN expression. Gastrocnemius muscle showed significant atrophy at 6-8 months, correlating with OA severity, whereas quadriceps atrophy was not significant. These findings establish CD1 mice as a robust spontaneous OA model that recapitulates the multi-tissue complexity of human disease. Because CD1 mice are globally available, cost-effective, genetically diverse and frequently, this model offers a practical and translationally relevant platform for investigating whole-joint organ mechanisms of OA progression and for evaluating therapies aimed at modifying disease across the entire joint.

papers.title: A miniaturized Arabidopsis thaliana - Botrytis cinerea seedling pathosystem and the GreenDayz workflow for longitudinal image-based phenotyping
papers.abstract: Plant-pathogen interactions are strongly influenced by host developmental stage, yet many Arabidopsis thaliana-Botrytis cinerea assays remain centred on mature rosette leaves and rely on inoculum loads that may exceed those involved in a primary infection. We established a miniaturized in vitro A. thaliana-B. cinerea seedling pathosystem initiated with a very low conidial dose (nominally ~25 conidia per plate) compatible with both destructive molecular sampling and repeated, non-destructive RGB imaging. The pathosystem was coupled to a low-cost smartphone photo station and to GreenDayZ Phenotyping, a guided image-analysis application with an intuitive graphical interface that standardizes longitudinal RGB image processing and extracts quantitative colour-based phenotypes. Together, the pathosystem and GreenDayZ Phenotyping provide an accessible and reproducible framework for longitudinal phenotyping of low-inoculum seedling infections, in which image-derived trajectories can be aligned with independent molecular readouts.

papers.title: Maternal obesity accelerates cardiomyocyte maturation and programs adult heart dysfunction in offspring
papers.abstract: Rationale: Maternal obesity increases cardiovascular risk in offspring, but the developmental mechanisms linking early-life metabolic stress to adult heart dysfunction remain poorly understood, and whether maternal obesity alters the postnatal maturation of the cardiomyocyte itself has not been addressed. Objective: To determine whether maternal high-fat diet alters the developmental trajectory of postnatal cardiomyocyte maturation and its functional consequences in adult offspring. Methods: In a rat model of maternal high-fat diet, longitudinal echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic phenotyping were combined with transcriptomic, lipidomic, and ultrastructural analyses across four postnatal stages. Results: Offspring exposed to maternal high-fat diet displayed accelerated postnatal cardiac maturation, with premature activation of contractile, calcium-handling and metabolic gene programs, concentric hypertrophy, and enhanced systolic performance in juvenile life. This precocious maturation was not sustained: by adulthood, ejection fraction and intrinsic myocardial contractility progressively declined, coinciding with disorganization of sarcomeres, intercalated discs, and excitation-contraction coupling proteins, in the absence of fibrosis, lipid accumulation or major mitochondrial respiratory dysfunction. Conclusions: These findings reveal accelerated cardiomyocyte maturation as a developmental mechanism linking maternal obesity to long-term cardiac vulnerability, with cardiomyocyte cytoarchitecture disruption emerging as an early hallmark that precedes overt systolic failure. Key words: Maternal obesity, DOHaD, postnatal cardiac maturation, cardiomyocyte cytoarchitecture, systolic dysfunction

papers.title: New whole slide image analysis method for detection and quantification of hepatocellular vacuolization in European flounder (Platichthys flesus) in multipollutant exposure context
papers.abstract: A new whole slide image analysis method was developed for hepatocellular vacuolization detection and quantification in European flounder (Platichthys flesus) liver. Histopathological quantification allows a better understanding of how contaminants and biotic factors might influence lesion pathogenesis in a multipollutant exposure context. One of the main findings is the significant difference in the extent of the pathology between the polluted and the control sites,with P. flesus sampled in the Seine estuary presenting a higher proportion of tissue affected by hepatocellular vacuolation (6.88 sd. 3.01%) compared to fish sampled in the Canche estuary (5.46 sd. 2.86%). This result is coherent with the previous qualitative histological assessment done on the same histological samples, it helps validate the method and brings new insight into the pathology intensity level with the level of contamination on each site. The other main finding is the potential synergetic effect of the pollutant mixture on the pathology. The multipollutant analysis showed a positive mixture effect on the proportion of tissue affected by hepatocellular vacuolation in fish from the Seine estuary, while this effect is not observed in fish sampled in the Canche estuary. This study highlights the benefits of developing novel bio-image analysis methods for environmental research. Histopathological diagnostic quantification allows a better understanding of the potential factors inducing and exacerbating the pathology, as well as the potential mixture effect in a context of multipollutant contamination.

papers.title: Mechano-activated synovial cells instigate OA-like disease progression in the absence of joint injury
papers.abstract: While altered tissue mechanics and cellular mechanoactivation accompany osteoarthritis, whether dysregulated mechanotransduction can initiate joint disease remains unclear. Here, we used intra-articular delivery of cell-penetrating TAT-Cre recombinase to locally perturb the actomyosin-Hippo mechanotransduction axis in mice. Deletion of Lats1/2, the negative regulators of the mechanosensitive transcriptional coactivators YAP and TAZ, induced sustained joint hyperalgesia, altered gait, synovial hyperplasia and fibrosis, vascular remodeling, and articular cartilage degeneration in the absence of a destabilizing injury. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed the emergence of Cthrc1+ matrix-remodeling fibroblasts and accumulation of Mrc1+Trem2+ macrophages during this pathological process. Histological analyses showed persistent contractile stromal remodeling and an early macrophage response that partially subsided over four weeks. Conversely, local deletion of Myh9/10, encoding the force-generating heavy chains of non-muscle myosin II, reduced hyperalgesia, synovial lining hyperplasia, alpha-SMA+ cell accumulation, and macrophage infiltration during post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) pathogenesis. However, this intervention did not detectably reduce cartilage degeneration at eight weeks. These findings establish synovial mechanotransduction as a causal driver of joint disease via immune-stromal remodeling and pain development. In addition, partial suppression of contractility separates symptomatic from structural outcomes in PTOA. Synovial mechanotransduction therefore represents a target for modulating pathological stromal-immune remodeling and joint pain.

papers.title: Progerin disrupts intestinal epithelial homeostasis by impairing mitochondrial metabolism and absorptive enterocyte maturation
papers.abstract: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) is a segmental premature ageing disease that predominantly affects tissues with high regenerative capacity. Although the intestine is the most rapidly self-renewing tissue of adult mammals, it has so far been considered only as a source of microbiota-derived disturbances in progeria, and whether the intestinal epithelium is itself a target of progerin remains unknown. Here, using the LmnaG609G/G609G and LmnaG609G/+ mouse models, intestinal organoids and single-cell RNA sequencing, we show that progerin is expressed in colonic enterocytes and in SMA+ subepithelial myofibroblasts of the stem-cell niche. Heterozygous progeria mice develop increased intestinal permeability from 30 weeks of age, reaching levels reported in physiologically aged (>20-month-old) mice. Progeria-derived intestinal organoids display reduced mitochondrial oxygen consumption, a compensatory increase in glycolysis and impaired crypt budding. Single-cell transcriptomics of the colonic epithelium and lamina propria revealed that, while lineage composition is preserved, progerin induces a coordinated reprogramming characterised by repression of oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial quality-control genes, including Nod2, activation of interferon, TNF-NF-kB and innate defence programs, and up-regulation of RNA-processing and chromatin-associated pathways. Trajectory analysis showed that progeria absorptive enterocytes selectively fail to reach terminal differentiation states and retain progenitor-like WNT, NOTCH and EGFR signatures, while lacking the mitochondrial programs required for maturation. Together, these findings identify the intestinal epithelium as a cell-intrinsic target of progerin and support a model in which mitochondrial insufficiency stalls absorptive enterocyte maturation and weakens the intestinal barrier, recapitulating, prematurely, key features of colon ageing.

papers.title: Asymptomatic colonization by Botrytis cinerea reveals polarized plant-fungus interfaces before widespread disease
papers.abstract: Botrytis cinerea is a necrotrophic pathogen whose destructive growth is typically studied under conditions that rapidly generate visible disease. Yet symptomless associations are well documented, the fungal and host processes operating before widespread tissue collapse remain poorly resolved. We developped an intact Arabidopsis thaliana seedling pathosystem that extends the interval between infection establishment and widespread visible disease. Fungal colonization was quantified using qPCR and a constitutively bioluminescent reporter strain, together with longitudinal plant phenotyping, hormone profiling and multiscale fluorescence microscopy. Substantial fungal colonization occurred while seedlings remained largely green and continued to grow, whereas robust whole seedling accumulation of salicylic and jasmonic acids occurred later. During this interval, B. cinerea displayed diverse tissue-associated infection morphologies. At individual contact sites, fungal walls showed heterogeneous exposure of chitin-associated epitopes, while host cells exhibited focal plasma-membrane polarization toward fungal contact sites, together with cortical actin reorganization. These results show that the interval preceding widespread visible disease is an active and spatially heterogeneous interaction state, in which substantial fungal development and highly organized local host responses are already established. Intact seedlings therefore provide a powerful system for resolving plant-pathogen interactions that are largely obscured in rapid disease assays.

papers.title: DTCAMD, a disease-associated truncated form of CRYAB in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a potential driver of subretinal fibrosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Subretinal fibrosis causes irreversible vision loss in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and remains poorly controlled by anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy. We investigated the role of B-crystallin (CRYAB) in angiogenic and fibrotic pathology and evaluated disease-associated CRYAB truncation as a therapeutic target. Methods: Aqueous humor from patients with nAMD was analyzed by quantitative proteomics and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. CRYAB function was assessed using knockout and knockdown approaches in a choroidal neovascularization (CNV) mouse model. CRYAB truncation and associated proteins were examined by immunoblotting, co-immunoprecipitation, and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). C-terminal truncation was further examined in mouse retinal tissue using antibodies generated against full-length CRYAB and its C-terminal region. Primary human retinal pigment epithelial (hRPE)-THP-1 co-cultures were used to examine CRYAB truncation under fibrosis-associated conditions. Pharmacological effects were tested using ({+/-})-threo-3-methylglutamic acid (T3MG) and 4-(2-aminoethyl)benzenesulfonyl fluoride hydrochloride (AEBSF). Results: CRYAB was upregulated in the aqueous humor of patients with nAMD. Higher CRYAB levels were associated with persistent lesions after initial anti-VEGF treatment. CRYAB knockout or knockdown reduced CNV pathology and decreased VEGFA and -smooth muscle actin (SMA) expression, without a significant substrain effect between C57BL/6N and C57BL/6J mice. A Ser45-phosphorylated truncated CRYAB species was detected in mouse laser-induced CNV model. We termed this species disease-associated truncated CRYAB in AMD (DTCAMD). Peptide mapping showed reproducible loss of distal C-terminal peptide coverage in truncated CRYAB. Consistent with this finding, C-terminal antibody recognition was reduced in CNV lesions. In hRPE-THP-1 co-cultures, DTCAMD accumulated with increased SMA expression. Proteomic analysis identified Prss1 as a candidate CRYAB-associated serine protease linked to truncation under CNV conditions. T3MG and AEBSF reduced DTCAMD-associated signals and CNV pathology. Conclusions: CRYAB contributes to angiogenic and fibrotic pathology in CNV. Disease-associated CRYAB truncation, particularly Ser45-phosphorylated DTCAMD, represents a potential therapeutic target for fibrotic remodeling in nAMD.

papers.title: Identification of the Col4a3-/- mouse as a model of chronic kidney disease-associated cachexia
papers.abstract: Background: Cachexia is a frequent complication of advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), i.e. renal cachexia, particularly in patients undergoing hemodialysis in whom it represents one of the strongest predictors of morbidity and mortality. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms leading to body wasting in CKD and management of cachectic patients are still poorly defined. To date, a preclinical mouse model of robust and reproducible CKD-associated cachexia is missing. Here, we assessed in a systematic manner the cachectic phenotype of the genetic Col4a3-/- mouse model of CKD. Methods: 129/SvJ Col4a3-/- male and female animals were monitored longitudinally until they developed kidney failure. Measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR), body composition and grip strength were recorded at baseline (6 weeks of age, before onset of kidney dysfunction) and at endpoint (CKD with weight loss or 12 weeks of age). The severity of CKD was confirmed by biochemical and histological analyses. Muscle atrophy was assessed via fiber cross-sectional area analysis, atrogene expression and transcriptomics. Adipose tissue wasting was assessed by measuring adipocyte area and proteins involved in lipid synthesis and breakdown. Liver acute phase response and systemic inflammation were evaluated by measuring circulating levels of key factors using ELISA. Results: Col4a3-/- animals developed CKD (decrease in mGFR: -85%, P<0.0001) and cachexia within 8-12 weeks of age. Cachexia was characterized by a progressive loss of body weight (-17.8% +/- 1.0, P<0.0001), lean (-8.2% +/- 2.0, P<0.0001) and fat mass (-66.5% +/- 4.7, P<0.0001) associated with reduced grip strength (-24.3% +/- 0.0, P=0.0002). At the tissue level, cachexia led to muscle atrophy and induction of atrogenes. Muscle transcriptomics further validated the cachectic phenotype of the Col4a3-/-, with 47% of genes altered in a similar manner with the well-established colon-C26 mouse model of cancer cachexia. It also revealed signatures that appeared more specific to renal cachexia. Adipose tissue wasting was characterized by a depletion in fat stores, consecutive to an imbalance between proteins involved in lipogenesis and lipolysis. Cachexia in this model was also associated with the induction of acute phase response in liver, elevated circulating levels of serum amyloid A and systemic inflammation, with the induction of established cachexia mediators (IL-6, GDF-15 P<0.0001). Both male and female mice developed cachexia. Conclusions: Our data highlight the potential of using the Col4a3-/- mouse model of CKD for the future study of renal cachexia, offering a more robust alternative to classically used models of partial nephrectomy or adenine-rich diet.

papers.title: Mutation in Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum F1C1 cytochrome p450 homologue impairs virulence through root but not through shoot of tomato plants
papers.abstract: Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum causes a lethal bacterial wilt disease in many plants. The pathogen enters through roots and systemically colonizes the xylem tissue, resulting in wilting and eventual death of the host. Using transposon mutagenesis followed by screening in tomato seedlings, we identified a mutant exhibiting virulence deficiency by root inoculation, but not by leaf inoculation. The mutation was recreated in the wild-type genome via natural transformation to prove the linkage of virulence deficiency with the transposon insertion. Whole genome sequencing revealed that the transposon insertion was in a cyp450 homologue, encoding cytochrome P450 monooxygenase. Two independent targeted mutations were generated in the cyp450 gene, and both the mutants recapitulated the root-specific virulence deficiency. The mutants rarely cause disease in mature plants following soil drenching but remained fully virulent upon petiole pricking inoculation. Complementation with the full length cyp450 gene amplified from the wild-type strain F1C1 restored virulence in the mutant. Compared to the wild-type F1C1, the cyp450 mutants exhibited greater sensitivity to tomato root extracts. HR-LCMS of tomato root extracts revealed the occurrence of several antimicrobial compounds. Cytochrome P450 enzymes are known to mediate the degradation or biosynthesis of diverse metabolites in bacteria. Considering the virulence difference due to the mode of inoculation, our findings indicate that cyp450 contributes to tissue-specific adaptation of the pathogen during infection has opened an avenue for integrating tissue metabolomics with bacterial wilt susceptibility research.

papers.title: UniMedSeg: Unified Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation via Uncertainty Guided Encoding and Frequency-Spatial Dual-Prompt Decoding
papers.abstract: Text-driven medical image segmentation demands unified models based on multi-modal learning, capable of processing diverse imaging modalities while providing spatially reliable prediction estimates for clinical practice. Nevertheless, existing vision-language model solutions suffer from poor domain generalization and exhibit limited capability for uncertainty estimation to model the cumulative unreliability of cross-modal alignment across network layers. In this paper, we propose UniMedSeg, a unified vision-language framework for multi-modal medical image segmentation built upon frozen pre-trained vision-language backbones. Our framework incorporates modality-aware adaptation, cross-layer uncertainty-guided encoding, and a frequency-spatial dual-prompt decoder, wherein the progressive uncertainty propagation mechanism of the encoder suppresses misleading cross-modal features, whereas the decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details in the frequency domain under dual textual prompts. Auxiliary losses further sharpen boundary representations and calibrate pixel-wise uncertainty maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniMedSeg preserves competitive in-domain segmentation performance, improves domain generalization, and yields clinically useful spatial risk estimation.

papers.title: Islet size and spatial organization govern endocrine cell composition throughout the human pancreas
papers.abstract: Stem cell-derived (SC) islets hold promise as a transformative therapy for type 1 diabetes (T1D). To enhance graft uniformity, SC-islet organoids are often dissociated and reaggregated into standardized sizes. However, how endocrine cell composition varies with islet size in native human islets remains largely unknown. Defining this relationship is essential for establishing physiological benchmarks for islet engineering for transplantation. In this study, we examined the relationships among islet size, endocrine cell composition, and spatial distribution throughout whole pancreata from 10 age-matched, non-diabetic male subjects. Insulin-, glucagon-, and somatostatin-positive endocrine cells were identified as single-, double-, and triple-hormone populations ranging from non-islet single endocrine cells and small clusters (niSSCs) to large islets. Approximately 80% of the total endocrine area was contained in islets positive for all three hormones. Islet size strongly correlated with endocrine composition. Specifically, larger islets had increased alpha-cell fractions and reduced beta-cell fractions, while delta-cell fractions were consistent across sizes. Spatial analysis revealed that niSSCs, mono-, and tri-hormone islets frequently exhibit a clustered distribution. Additionally, tri-hormone islets were positioned near the core of the pancreas, whereas mono-somatostatin islets were often localized in the periphery. These findings were consistent across all three pancreatic regions (head, body and tail).

papers.title: Polyphyletic origin and horizontal exchange drive the emergence of a novel resistance-breaking Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lactucae race
papers.abstract: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lactucae (Fola), the cause of lettuce fusarium wilt, poses an increasing threat to global production due to the rapid emergence of resistance breaking isolates. However, the evolutionary origins and mechanisms underpinning this diversification remain poorly understood. We characterised 103 Fola isolates using molecular profiling, selecting ten key isolates for long-read whole-genome sequencing and performed in planta virulence assays for selected isolates. This included the first assemblies for Fola2 and Fola3, recent resistance-breaking variants and a highly divergent isolate from France designated as a putative novel race, FolaX. Phylogenomic analysis revealed that Fola is polyphyletic, with lettuce pathogenicity acquired independently across divergent F. oxysporum clades. Despite this, all lineages share a conserved "PanFola" effector set with near-identical sequences, indicating extensive horizontal gene transfer. Resistance-breaking Fola variants within established races were linked to copy number variations and targeted deletions, such as the loss of the SIX8/PSE1 locus in Fola4+. Conversely, FolaX possessed a divergent core genome and a chimeric accessory genome derived from multiple Fola lineages via segmental chromosome transfer and transposon-mediated reshuffling. Our findings highlight the remarkable evolutionary plasticity of Fola and the need for breeding strategies that address the dynamic nature of effector repertoires.

papers.title: Macrophages from Holstein and Normande cows respond differently to Escherichia coli and Streptococcus uberis
papers.abstract: Macrophages, alongside mammary epithelial cells, are major contributors to the innate immune response triggered by bacterial invasion of the mammary gland. To investigate breed-specific immune mechanisms, we stimulated monocyte-derived macrophages from Holstein and Normande cattle with Escherichia coli and Streptococcus uberis, two major mastitis pathogens. We monitored bacterial survival using [methode] and profiled gene expression via RNA-seq. E. coli exhibited significantly higher survival 6 hours post-infection compared to S. uberis (p 1), versus only 813 for S. uberis. Qualitative differences were also observed: genes such as CCL2 and CSF1 were uniquely induced by S. uberis. Additionally, macrophages from Holstein and Normande cattle showed distinct expression profiles: 185, 45, and 174 genes were differentially expressed at steady state or after E. coli or S. uberis stimulation, respectively. These genes were enriched in immune-related pathways. Overall, our results demonstrate a stronger response to E. coli, although S. uberis specifically induces a subset of genes. The observed breed-specific differences may reflect underlying immune mechanisms that could influence disease susceptibility, warranting further functional validation.

papers.title: A Weight Loss Fibrotic Response in Visceral Fat Is Driven by Defective Lysosome-Dependent Collagenolysis
papers.abstract: Obesity induces pathological remodeling of white adipose tissue (WAT), including chronic inflammation and fibrosis, which drive metabolic dysfunction. Although weight loss (WL) is the cornerstone of obesity treatment and improves systemic metabolic health, its impact on WAT remodeling remains incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity followed by nutritional weight loss, we show that visceral WAT (vWAT) fails to fully recover despite normalization of body weight and marked metabolic improvment. Notably, vWAT fibrosis persists and continues to progress after WL. This occurs while extracellular matrix (ECM) production by adipose progenitor cells is markedly reduced following WL, explaining why pharmacological inhibition of ECM synthesis fails to prevent fibrosis during WL. Instead, we observed impaired collagen degradation by both progenitor cells and macrophages, along with lysosomal dysfunction, during WL. This suggests that defective ECM degradation, rather than continued ECM production, underlies fibrosis persistence and aggravation during WL. Together, these findings identify impaired collagenolysis as a critical barrier to adipose tissue recovery after WL and suggest that enhancing ECM clearance, rather than inhibiting ECM synthesis, may represent a more effective therapeutic strategy to restore adipose tissue function.

papers.title: Transient tubular membrane injury is converted into persistent fibrosis through a macrophage-fibroblast relay
papers.abstract: A central unresolved problem in acute kidney injury (AKI) is how a transient epithelial insult is converted into persistent fibrotic repair that drives progression toward chronic kidney disease. Although tubular, immune and stromal responses are individually well recognized, the mechanistically continuous relay linking these three compartments has remained unresolved. Here we define a directional information-conversion pathway spanning injured tubular epithelial cells, macrophages and fibroblasts. Time-resolved single-cell profiling identified a TREM2/SPP1 macrophage state that emerged as post-ischemic repair became fibrotic. Tubular injury remodeled phosphatidylserine (PS) species, increased oxidized PS and PS externalization, and generated a membrane-lipid context for TREM2 sensing, supported by PS masking, defined liposomes and orthogonal binding assays. Structure-function analysis separated R47-dependent phospholipid recognition from K183-dependent DAP12 coupling, linking membrane damage to SYK activation and NF-kB/AP-1-driven Spp1 transcription. Macrophage-derived SPP1 then activated ITGAV/ITGB1-associated FAK-SMAD2/3 signaling, fibroblast contraction and matrix production. Crucially, repair-phase SPP1 neutralization and post-injury Cx3cr1-lineage Trem2 deletion attenuated fibrosis, with delayed Trem2 deletion protective in both ischemic and obstructive injury. Human single-cell, spatial, urinary and tissue analyses showed cross-species and cross-scale convergence. These findings resolve how transient tubular membrane damage is successively transformed across three cellular compartments into persistent, yet interruptible, fibrotic repair.

papers.title: Toll-like receptor expression across histological states of Epidermodysplasia Verruciformis
papers.abstract: Epidermodysplasia verruciformis (EV) is characterized by susceptibility to cutaneous {beta}-human papillomaviruses, persistent viral lesions and an increased risk of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). We investigated whether expression of Toll-like receptors 3, 4, 5 and 9 (TLR3, TLR4, TLR5 and TLR9) differs across histological states within EV. Immunoreactivity was quantified by digital H-score using QuPath in 97 specimens from 28 patients, comprising 13 lesion-free skin samples, 15 flat warts and 69 cSCCs. Prespecified comparisons evaluated flat wart versus lesion-free skin, cSCC versus non-neoplastic tissue and invasive versus in situ cSCC, with invasive tumour differentiation assessed secondarily. Patient-clustered generalized estimating equations and false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction were used for inference. After correction for multiple testing, TLR9 H-scores were higher in flat warts than in lesion-free skin ({beta}=60.58; q=0.0332). Compared with non-neoplastic tissue, cSCC showed lower TLR3 ({beta}=-81.40; q=0.00745), higher TLR4 ({beta}=55.59; q=0.04793) and lower TLR9 expression ({beta}=-34.80; q=0.03412). TLR5 showed a nominal increase in cSCC that did not meet the FDR threshold. None of the four receptors differed significantly between invasive and in situ cSCC, and no differentiation trend remained significant after FDR correction. These findings show receptor-specific differences in TLR expression across histological states of EV, particularly involving TLR3, TLR4 and TLR9, although the diagnostic and prognostic significance of these tissue patterns remains to be established.

papers.title: Monothiol glutaredoxin DaGrxB couples iron homeostasis with redox balance to orchestrate development and virulence in the peach shoot blight fungus Diaporthe amygdali
papers.abstract: Peach shoot blight (PSB), caused by Diaporthe amygdali, is one of the most devastating fungal diseases affecting peach production worldwide. Glutaredoxins (Grxs) are ubiquitous redox-regulatory proteins involved in antioxidant defense and iron metabolism, yet their functions in phytopathogenic fungi remain largely unknown. Here, we identified four Grxs (DaGrxA-DaGrxD) in D. amygdali. Among them, DaGrxB, a monothiol glutaredoxin, is the sole member essential for vegetative growth, asexual reproduction and virulence. DaGrxB interacts with iron-regulatory transcription factors DaHapX and DaSreA and modulates their activities via iron-dependent nucleocytoplasmic shuttling, coordinating iron acquisition and storage gene expression. During infection, D. amygdali encounters a biphasic iron environment: an inherently iron-limited host environment at early stages (1-2 dpi) followed by host-mediated iron excess (3-4 dpi), and DaGrxB is essential for navigating this transition. Consistently, deletion of either DaHAPX or DaSREA significantly reduced virulence, confirming that iron homeostasis is a critical determinant of D. amygdali virulence. Notably, deletion of DaGRXB disrupts Fe-S cluster biosynthesis, causing mitochondrial Fe2+ accumulation, impaired aconitase activity, and reduced ATP production, which triggers constitutive activation of the GSH-dependent antioxidant system, with elevated GSH/GSSG ratios, increased GR and GST activities, and reduced H2O2 levels. Exogenous GSH and H2O2 depletion both reduced virulence, suggesting that disturbed redox balance directly contributes to attenuated virulence. Additionally, the Trx domain assists the Grx domain in nucleocytoplasmic translocation through intramolecular interactions. Finally, LDH-delivered dsRNA targeting DaGRXB effectively controls PSB. Collectively, these findings reveal how a monothiol glutaredoxin integrates iron homeostasis, redox balance and virulence in a plant pathogen, providing a foundation for RNAi-based disease management.

papers.title: Vascular endothelial cadherin remodeling is associated with endothelial barrier dysfunction in chronic subdural hematoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) remains a significant and increasingly prevalent cause of morbidity in older adults. Disease progression is sustained by de novo formed highly vascularized pseudomembranes and a persistent cycle of fluid accumulation and hematoma expansion. Although inflammatory and angiogenic pathways have been implicated in cSDH pathogenesis, the endothelial mechanisms underlying persistent vascular leak remain poorly understood. We investigated the cSDH vascular microenvironment in human patients and examined the role of vascular endothelial cadherin (VECAD) remodeling in cSDH endothelial dysfunction. Methods: Human cSDH membranes and fluid were evaluated by multiplex profiling, histology, immunofluorescence, immunoprecipitation, western blotting and exploratory bulk RNA sequencing. A human brain endothelial cell (HBEC) line was exposed to patient-derived cSDH fluid to assess VECAD remodeling, endothelial barrier permeability, and proliferation. Results: Multiplex profiling of patient-derived cSDH fluid detected mediators associated with endothelial cell (EC) activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation, and angiogenesis. In patient pseudomembranes, discontinuous VECAD coincided with erythrocyte extravasation. Two hyperdense (high-risk) specimens showed more extensive disruption than the hypodense (low-risk) specimen while vessel counts appeared similar. Bulk RNA sequencing identified an angiogenic environment and enrichment in cadherin regulation. A soluble VECAD (sVECAD) isoform was detected in cSDH fluid. Exposure of HBECs to patient-derived cSDH fluid increased EC proliferation, cytoplasmic VECAD (cVECAD) accumulation, and EC barrier permeability. Concurrent dexamethasone or minocycline treatment attenuated VECAD cleavage. Conclusions: VECAD disruption is a prominent feature of cSDH and is associated with EC barrier dysfunction. These findings support further evaluation of soluble VECAD as a candidate biomarker and of junction-preserving pathways as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Pathogenic transcriptional reprogramming of fibro-adipogenic progenitors in mice with FOP and its mitigation by inhibition of ACVR1 and activin A
papers.abstract: Individuals with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the bone morphogenetic protein receptor ACVR1 (also known as ALK2), experience progressive and severely debilitating endochondral heterotopic ossification (HO). Previous studies have identified fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) as a major cellular source of HO in FOP mouse models. Here, we used mRNA sequencing of FAPs isolated from injured muscle of FOP mice to capture the earliest gene expression changes associated with the transformation of muscle tissues into bone. Whereas the transcriptomes of mutant and wild-type FAPs were indistinguishable prior to injury and at 1 day post injury, dramatic dysregulation of gene expression was observed at 3 and 5 days after injury. Surprisingly, gene expression changes suggested early specification of osteochondral lineages by 3 days post injury, approximately 3 to 4 days before the appearance of histologically identifiable cartilage. We identified dysregulation of genes encoding components of major signaling pathways, cell cycle regulators, extracellular matrix components, and hypoxia response mediators, and showed that these gene expression changes are temporally associated with abnormal population growth of mutant FAPs. We further demonstrated that treatment of FOP mice with either an anti-activin A monoclonal antibody or the ACVR1 kinase inhibitor BLU-782 (IPN60130; fidrisertib) normalized the expression of the majority of dysregulated FAP genes. However, the relative efficacy of the drugs differed, and distinct sets of overlapping genes were normalized by the treatments. The substantial transcriptional changes caused by these drugs in FAPs from normally regenerating muscle were also enumerated and described. These findings define early transcriptional events associated with pathogenic FAP reprogramming and provide a molecular framework for understanding the shared and distinct effects of activin A and ACVR1 inhibition.

papers.title: RNA-guided contrastive learning enhances patient-level prediction from histology
papers.abstract: Predicting molecular receptor status, including estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) could reduce reliance on costly immunohistochemistry, but image-only models have no access to the transcriptomic programs that define these subtypes. Here we show that coupling a whole-slide vision transformer (GigaPath) with bulk RNA-sequencing profiles through a training-time-only contrastive objective improves receptor-status classification from WSIs alone, without requiring any RNA-seq data at inference. Rather than training a dedicated bulk-transcriptomics encoder, we purpose the gene-sentence encoding and pretrained text encoder from BioBERT1 and apply them to bulk RNA-seq profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cancer cohort (TCGA-BRCA). Under five-fold cross-validation, this RNA-guided pre-training consistently improved AUROC for ER, PR, and HER2 relative to a contrastive-pre-training-free baseline and reproducibly introduced receptor-relevant structure into the learned slide representation. However, evaluation on independent external cohorts revealed a striking, receptor-dependent divergence: gains for ER and PR, both governed by broad, multi-gene luminal transcriptional programs, generalized robustly, whereas the apparent AUROC improvement for HER2, driven by focal ERBB2 amplification rather than a coordinated transcriptional signature, masked a severe loss of classification sensitivity at the operating threshold. These findings establish training-time transcriptomic supervision as a practical route to enhancing histology-only molecular subtyping, while showing that gene-selection strategy, and not model architecture alone, determines which molecular alterations such supervision can teach a vision model to recognize.

papers.title: Characterization of Congestive Heart Failure Phenotype in a Murine Model of JAK2V617F-positive Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
papers.abstract: Background: Murine models are widely used to investigate cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet many established models rely on invasive surgery or genetic manipulation to induce hyperlipidemia and therefore may not fully capture the gradual cardiovascular consequences of mutant hematopoiesis. Tie2-Cre/-FF1/- (Tie2FF1) mice express JAK2V617F mutation in both hematopoietic and endothelial cells and develop spontaneous CVD on a standard chow diet. Methods: We applied a comprehensive, non-invasive cardiovascular phenotyping protocol to 1-year-old Tie2FF1 mice and age-matched controls. Assessments included transthoracic echocardiography, coronary flow reserve by Doppler ultrasound, quantitative analysis of coronary arteriolar structure and perivascular fibrosis, endocardial histology and subendocardial collagen deposition, and histologic evaluation of pulmonary and hepatic congestion. Results: Tie2FF1 mice demonstrated left ventricular dilation, increased cardiac mass, and mildly reduced systolic function without obstructive epicardial coronary disease. Coronary microvascular remodeling was evident by arteriolar narrowing and increased perivascular fibrosis, while coronary flow reserve was markedly reduced in an exploratory cohort. Endocardial endothelial disruption and increased subendocardial fibrosis were also observed. In addition, Tie2FF1 mice showed increased lung and liver weights, pulmonary fluid accumulation, alveolar septal thickening, pulmonary vascular fibrosis, hepatic sinusoidal dilatation, and centrilobular hepatocyte swelling, providing objective evidence of clinically relevant heart failure. Significance: These findings establish Tie2FF1 mice as a spontaneous, non-invasive model with features of coronary microvascular and endocardial endothelial dysfunction and heart failure with mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. The integrated approach described here provides a practical framework for comprehensive murine cardiovascular phenotyping beyond traditional atherosclerosis- and surgery-based models.

papers.title: Evaluating the Transferability of Pathology Foundation Models Across Cancer-related H&E Neurodegeneration-related Immunohistochemical Classification Tasks
papers.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) have rapidly become dominant in artificial intelligence and are increasingly being adopted in computational pathology. Numerous pathology-specific FMs have been developed and evaluated for a variety of downstream tasks, most commonly using frozen image embeddings with linear probes. While a pathology FM, at least implicitly suggests broad reusability across tasks, the transferability of these models to neurodegenerative disease-related tasks remains largely unexplored. In this study, we evaluated fourteen frozen feature extractors, including general-vision and pathology FMs, across four pathology image classification datasets spanning two specialized neurodegenerative disease immuno-histochemistry (IHC) tasks (Tau neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) and amyloid-{beta} plaque classification) and two cancer-related hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) tasks (the breast tissue BACH dataset and the multi-tissue TIL dataset). The cancer-related H&E datasets represent tasks more closely aligned with the predominant pretraining domain of many current pathology FMs, whereas the neurodegenerative IHC datasets represent a more specialized domain with limited representation in existing FM pretraining cohorts. Frozen embedding linear probes were compared against a conventional supervised ResNet-50 convolutional neural network (CNN) trained directly on image tiles using identical train, validation, and test splits. Across both neurodegenerative IHC datasets, the supervised CNN substantially outperformed all frozen FM linear probes. In contrast, pathology FMs achieved performance comparable to, and in some cases exceeding, the supervised CNN across the two cancer-related H&E datasets, with UNI2-h achieving the highest performance on BACH and several pathology FMs performing on par with the CNN on the larger TIL dataset. Furthermore, a supervised CNN trained using only 1% of the Tau NFT training data (1,938 tiles) still exceeded the performance of the best frozen FM linear probe trained on the complete dataset. Together, these results suggest the transferability of frozen pathology FMs may depend strongly on how well the downstream task is represented by their pretraining domain. These findings demonstrate frozen pathology FMs transfer effectively to the cancer-related H&E tasks evaluated here but may be less effective for specialized neurodegenerative IHC tasks less well represented in current FM pretraining cohorts. Expanding pathology FM pretraining datasets to include a broader range of disease domains and staining modalities may therefore improve transferability to specialized pathology applications. Our findings also highlight the continued importance of conventional supervised learning and motivate future work investigating nonlinear probes and end-to-end FM fine-tuning.

papers.title: Keto-gluconeogenic metabolic axis mirrors renal homeostasis and post-injury response in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Metabolic disturbance is a key feature in acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). The kidney highly depends on fatty acid metabolism; how renal cells rewire metabolism upon AKI and CKD transition remained unclear. Here, we combine spatial transcriptomics with biochemical analyses to characterize metabolic changes and intercellular interactions during AKI to CKD transition. Using aristolochic acid model of CKD, we spatio-temporally correlated changes in structure and function with metabolic profile during AKI to CKD transition. Surprisingly, keto-gluconeogenic metabolic axis was highly enriched in healthy kidney and paralleled injury phase transitions. Intercellular interaction analysis associated a subtype of macrophage with the drift to chronicity. Online scRNAseq datasets analysis confirmed altered keto-gluconeogenic metabolic pathways in ischemia-reperfusion injured mouse kidneys and AKI and CKD human kidney biopsies compared to healthy controls. This study identifies a metabolic axis transcriptionally mirroring renal homeostasis and injury responses, and tubulo-interstitial interactions that can be targeted to mitigate AKI to CKD transition.

papers.title: Identification of Novel Inhibitors of JEV RdRp as Potent Antiviral Drugs: Targeting NS5-NS3 Protein Interaction
papers.abstract: Japanese Encephalitis Virus (JEV) belongs to the Flavivirus family, and the RNA dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) domain located at the C terminus of non structural protein 5 (NS5) regulates de novo viral genome synthesis. The conserved priming loop inserted in the thumb domain of RDRP initiates de novo genome synthesis. Interestingly, the reported replication process initiates with an interaction between NS5 (methyltransferase/RDRP) and NS3 (protease/helicase), and inhibiting this interaction directly correlates with the inhibition of viral replication. The function of the priming loop in the context of the NS5 NS3 interaction is not yet known. In this study, we studied the priming loop function in the NS5 NS3 interaction and viral replication. Using a structure based drug design approach, we screened the Maybridge compound library against the RdRp priming loop and identified 15 candidate compounds based on binding energy. Among them, DSHS00151 showed significant dose dependent inhibition of the NS5 NS3 interaction with an IC50 of 3.5 micromolar in the mammalian two hybrid assay, inhibited viral infectivity with an IC50 of 2.54 micromolar, and reduced viral RNA load with an IC50 of 2.9 micromolar, compared to CD10712. Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that DSHS00151 exhibits stronger and more stable binding with the priming loop residues (790 to 812) compared to CD10712. The molecular mechanism suggested by the docking of the NS5 and NS3 proteins showed that the priming loop tends to rotate toward the NS3 protein to stabilize the complex, and compound binding restricts this loop rotation, thus compromising the stability of the NS5 and NS3 complex and affecting viral replication. Overall, our study validated the function of the NS5 priming loop as an allosteric site, and compounds binding to this allosteric site belong to the Non Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTI) class of inhibitors, which disrupt the NS5 and NS3 interaction and could be developed as novel anti JEV therapeutics.

papers.title: Quantitative Model of the Ocular Immune Response during Seasonal Allergic Conjunctivitis
papers.abstract: Allergic conjunctivitis is an inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by allergen; it is common disorder affecting up to 40% of the population. In this work, we study seasonal allergic conjunctivitis (SAC), also called "hay fever eyes", which is caused by exposure to airborne pollens. We develop a mathematical model quantifying the ocular immune system response to the allergens. First, we present a simplified qualitative description of the immunopathogenesis of SAC. Then, we express each chosen immunopathological mechanism mathematically to construct a system of thirty-one ordinary differential equations. We compare summary statistics of the predicted observable immune signals to experimental measurements and find our model captures key qualitative features of SAC progression. We then compare our predicted time series of histamine concentration to symptom scores and find a strong correlation suggesting the model predicts relevant clinically trends. Next, we calibrate the model through multi-step process. We find the most influential parameters are the production and depletion rates of IL-4, and the production rates of IL-5 and IL-8. These cytokines are targeted in treatments for asthma, atopic dermatitis, and severe eosinophilic associated disorder and suggest potential therapeutic targets for SAC. Our calibrated model mimics most of the summary statistics of the experimentally observable immune signals with discrepancies for IL-5 and IL-13 indicating that additional immunopathological mechanisms could be important.

papers.title: Autophagic flux is increased in peripheral blood mononuclear cells in atherosclerotic vascular disease and associates inversely with adverse cardiovascular events
papers.abstract: Background: Autophagy is a homeostatic pathway supporting stress adaptation and is dysregulated in atherosclerosis. Its potential as a biomarker or therapeutic target in atherosclerotic vascular disease (ASVD) remains incompletely defined. We measured autophagic flux in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) or carotid stenosis (CS), compared with healthy controls, and explored clinical outcome associations. Methods: Ninety-four patients with PAD or CS and 19 healthy controls were studied. Autophagic flux was quantified from fresh blood using a validated ex vivo chloroquine inhibition ELISA measuring LC3BII accumulation. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major adverse limb events (MALE) were ascertained over a median follow up of 828 days. Results: The ASVD cohort comprised claudication (n = 16), chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI; n = 49), and CS (n = 29). Autophagic flux was higher in ASVD than controls (mean 281.4 vs. 182.3 ng LC3BII/mg protein/h; p < 0.0001) and remained independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Within CLTI, concurrent infection was associated with lower flux (p = 0.001), approaching control levels (p = 0.327). In CLTI, higher flux quartiles were associated with lower MACE risk, most strongly for quartile 3 (hazard ratio 0.07 vs. quartile 1, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.50; p = 0.009). Conclusion: Autophagic flux is elevated in PBMCs from ASVD patients, independent of age and sex. Attenuated flux in CLTI with concurrent infection may indicate autophagic exhaustion in advanced disease. The association between higher flux and lower MACE in CLTI suggests prognostic utility, warranting evaluation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Dysregulated Platelet GPIb alpha - VWF Signalling in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm formation and Progression
papers.abstract: Background: Platelets are critical drivers of thrombo-inflammatory responses in different cardiovascular diseases. Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, life-threatening vascular disorder mainly characterised by chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation, and the formation of a platelet-rich intraluminal thrombus (ILT). Experimental and clinical evidence identified platelets as main players in AAA pathology as evidenced by elevated platelet activation and procoagulant activity that critically contribute to AAA progression. Methods: The present study investigated the contribution of glycoprotein (GP)Ib alpha, the von Willebrand factor (VWF)-binding subunit of the platelet GPIb-IX-V complex, to AAA initiation and progression in experimental AAA using the ePPE mouse model and in patients. Results: Genetic ablation of platelet GPIb alpha significantly attenuated early aneurysm expansion in experimental AAA, indicating a critical role for GPIb alpha during the initial stages of aneurysm development. This initial effect was compensated at later time points showing no differences in aneurysm progression between groups. Notably, genetic deletion of GPIb alpha induced a constitutively hyperactive platelet phenotype already in naive mice that was further amplified during experimental AAA. This elevated platelet hyperactivity was mainly due to increased GPVI activation of platelets 28 days post-surgery. To assess the clinical relevance, spatial profiles of human ILT specimens from patients with AAA were analysed. In the ILT, we detected a highly compartmentalised distribution of GPIb alpha and VWF with pronounced enrichment within the luminal layer. In parallel, circulating VWF activity as well as platelet surface expression of GPIb alpha were significantly increased in patients with AAA. Conclusion: Collectively, these findings identify a dysregulated GPIb alpha-VWF axis in human AAA pathology, mainly characterised by enhanced platelet GPIb alpha surface expression and increased activity of circulating VWF.
